Subject: Production: sudden latency / 504s this morning

Hi Tessa / Jordan,

We started seeing a big jump in generation latency for our live endpoints around 08:55 ET. p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s and p99s are spiking above 3s. A handful of requests are returning 504s. This started abruptly (request ids attached).

Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side and whether an emergency mitigation is available? We have a weekly business review coming up and need a status ASAP.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: sudden latency / 504s this morning

Thanks for the ping — quick summary of what we see so far from the serving-side logs and traces:

- Timeline: ~09:00 ET a scheduled cache eviction job (tenant-agnostic eviction policy) rolled out to a subset of hosted clusters as part of a housekeeping change.
- Effect: eviction aggressively invalidated prefix/KV cache entries which resulted in an increased rate of cold KV fetches and longer token-generation latencies (the cold-path induces additional front-end->kv round trips and serialization).
- Evidence: samples from the request ids show cache-miss ratios jumping from ~5% -> 48% for affected prefixes; KV fetch latencies correlate with p99 spikes.

Immediate mitigations proposed (can action in 10-25m):
1) Temporarily disable the new eviction window for the affected cluster pool (we can scope by tenant id for FinSight) — reduces cold misses immediately.
2) Trigger targeted pre-warm for FinSight's common prefixes (warm recently evicted keys).
3) If needed, route FinSight traffic to a pinned warm node pool while we stabilize.

I'll try mitigation (1) now and report back. Keeping this high priority.

- Rishi
Director, Inference Platform

Subject: Executive FYI: Hosted API p95/p99 spikes affecting FinSight — mitigation in flight

Aditya / Evelyn — FYI and short summary: FinSight reported a production p95/p99 regression and 504s at ~08:55 ET. Engineering suspects an aggressive prefix/KV eviction job that rolled earlier this morning is the primary cause. Rishi is executing a scoped disable + pre-warm now.

Customer impact: intermittent timeouts for a subset of paying users (FinSight flagged for Business Review). We are treating as S1 and tracking for an SLA credit request. I will share a postmortem plan after we stabilise.

- Tessa
VP, Customer Success
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-28T14:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: sudden latency / 504s this morning — mitigation update

Update: disabled eviction window for the affected clusters at 13:45 ET and kicked off a targeted pre-warm for the top 250 FinSight prefixes. Early metrics: p95 improved from ~1.2s -> ~300ms within 12 minutes; p99 improved but still has residual tail ~800-900ms for certain heavy prefixes. 504s have dropped to near-zero.

Next steps:
- Continue pre-warm for another 45m and monitor p99 tail.
- Create a scoped rollback/coordinate with infra to revert the eviction rollout; add tenant-scoping to eviction policy to prevent tenant-wide cold storms.
- We will prepare a short postmortem and remediation plan (including opt-out knobs for certain enterprise tenants).

I'll keep the dashboard feed live; attaching a short runbook clip showing the eviction toggle we used.

- Rishi
